claims.text: Intrinsic lattice anharmonicity in HfNbTaTiZr produces non-linear thermal expansion.
Non-linear thermal expansion directly modulates dislocation climb and slip kinetics in HfNbTaTiZr.
Coupling between lattice anharmonicity and dislocation kinetics governs the alloy's high-temperature stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior.
Elevated-temperature refractory high-entropy alloys can exhibit atypical temperature-dependent elastic and plastic deformation behavior.
The cited elevated-temperature elastic-deformation findings apply directly to HfNbTaTiZr.
Annealing and homogenization minimize compositional segregation and phase inhomogeneity in the tested HfNbTaTiZr samples.
In-situ neutron diffraction can track lattice strain and determine elastic moduli during elevated-temperature deformation of a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Anharmonic effects are pronounced in HfNbTaTiZr between 600 °C and 1250 °C.
Anharmonic atomic vibrations cause deviations from linear thermal expansion.
Thermal-expansion deviations alter local strain fields and reduce activation barriers for dislocation climb and slip.
Changes in climb and slip kinetics caused by anharmonicity modify elastic moduli and creep response.
The degree of thermal-expansion non-linearity will correlate with changes in elastic moduli and creep rates.
Samples with larger deviations from linear thermal expansion will exhibit greater dislocation activity and altered stress–strain curves and creep parameters.
A harmonic-lattice approximation provides a baseline of linear thermal expansion and standard creep and elastic behavior.
Below 600 °C, HfNbTaTiZr should show approximately linear thermal expansion and conventional dislocation kinetics.
Isotopic substitution or thermal-treatment controls can isolate anharmonic contributions from other high-temperature deformation mechanisms.
